restrictions: Generic van Oorschot-Wiener distinguished-point collision search on one processor; every instruction charged under collision-frontier-v5 with C=1355.

Messages are exactly 32 bytes, msg(x)=LE32(x); iteration f(x)=H(msg(x)) on the complete fixed-zero-state five-round SHA3-256 sponge with 0x06 padding, injective so any f-collision is an ordinary collision of two distinct messages.

Distinguished point iff low 32 output bits are zero (theta=2^-32); maximum chain L=2^40; evaluation budget K0=65300*2^112 plus at most L to complete the final chain; distinguished-record cap 2^98 (bounds the number of distinguished points and hence per-chain lookup work).
Worst-case charged time below 2^128.023 for every run; success probability at least 0.39 under declared heuristic H-RF only; all other bounds are heuristic-free.
One run, no restart; failed trials, abandoned chains, the relocation walk and final re-hash verification are all charged. No certificate, experiment, precomputed collision, or nonuniform advice.
The nominal reference identifier does not assert an improvement over an established attack or security bound.

heuristics.statement: An evaluation of f = H . msg at a point not previously evaluated returns a value uniform on {0,1}^256, independent of the algorithm's coins and of all previously observed values. Used only to lower-bound the success probability; the time, memory and preprocessing bounds hold for every run without it.
heuristics.scope: The at most K0 < 2^128 evaluations of f in one run on the fixed complete five-round SHA3-256 map (target sha3-256-r5-prefix-v1).
heuristics.extrapolation: From standard modelling of a fixed cryptographic permutation's output as uniform to the specific five-round map; no proof of ideal behaviour is claimed, and the required success budget changes log2(T) by well under one bit even under a constant-factor correction.
heuristics.limitations: A modelling assumption, plausible rather than established; a proven bias in the five-round image distribution could change the exact success probability. Only the 0.39 figure depends on it, not correctness or the time bound.
